option_relations.rationale: The patient's medical history of IgG λ-type multiple myeloma and the presence of amyloid deposits in the skin biopsy suggest a diagnosis of AL (primary) amyloidosis, which is equivalent to Multiple Myeloma-associated Amyloidosis.
Bullous amyloidosis can be a subtype of systemic amyloidosis, which is related to Multiple Myeloma-associated Amyloidosis.
Systemic amyloidosis (AL type) is equivalent to Multiple Myeloma-associated Amyloidosis, as both refer to the deposition of amyloid proteins in tissues due to multiple myeloma.

Acquired Cutaneous Amyloidosis (Secondary to Multiple Myeloma) can be a subtype of Multiple Myeloma-associated Amyloidosis, as it refers to the deposition of amyloid proteins in the skin due to multiple myeloma.
